description: Welcome to ZYTHERA! We are a team of two enthusiastic students passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. As beginners, we are eager to learn, explore NASA's open data, and develop creative solutions to real-world problems. We value teamwork, curiosity, and innovation, and look forward to building a meaningful project while learning from mentors and fellow participants.
summary:
SPACE RELICS: The Machines That Stayed Behind

SPACE RELICS is an interactive educational storytelling website developed by Team ZYTHERA for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores the stories of human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars, showing how each object represents an important part of space exploration.

The website features a searchable mission archive, an interactive Moon and Mars artifact map, a mission timeline, a comparison of different missions, and a short space quiz. Through NASA mission images, historical information, and linked research sources, visitors can discover the purpose of these machines, the missions behind them, and the discoveries they helped make possible.

Our project addresses the challenge by turning information about space equipment left behind into an engaging and accessible learning experience. It is important because these relics are more than abandoned hardware: they preserve scientific knowledge, engineering lessons, and the history of humanity's exploration beyond Earth.
details:
SPACE RELICS is an interactive educational storytelling website developed by Team ZYTHERA for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It explores human-made equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars and shares the stories behind these important objects.

The website allows visitors to explore a relic archive, discover artifacts through an interactive Moon and Mars map, follow a mission timeline, compare space missions and test their knowledge through an interactive quiz. Each feature helps users understand the purpose of the equipment, the missions involved and the scientific discoveries they contributed to.

The project benefits students, educators and space enthusiasts by making space exploration history more accessible, engaging and enjoyable. Its intended impact is to increase awareness of the scientific and historical value of space mission equipment and inspire curiosity about planetary exploration.

We developed the website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript. GitHub was used for source-code management and team collaboration, while GitHub Pages was used for public hosting. We also used NASA-related mission information, images and supporting resources.

The creative aspect of SPACE RELICS is its storytelling approach. Instead of presenting only technical facts, it transforms the stories of these machines into an interactive learning experience. Our team considered information accuracy, educational value, accessibility, user experience, visual design and ease of navigation throughout development.

SPACE RELICS reminds us that even when a mission ends, the stories and knowledge behind its machines remain valuable.
